Synapse's mitigation for malicious `multipart/form-data` requests (see https://github.com/element-hq/synapse/security/advisories/GHSA-rfq8-j7rh-8hf2) can be bypassed by varying the case of the `Content-Type` header.

When processing such a maliciously-crafted request, Synapse quickly exhausts all available memory, becoming unresponsive and/or being terminated, denying service to other users.

### Patches

Update to Synapse 1.157.2 or later, which corrects the mitigation to deny such requests.

See the table below for patched versions of [Element Server Suite](https://element.io/en/server-suite), including Long-Term Support (LTS) versions.
|  | 25.10 LTS | 26.4 LTS | Latest |
|:--|--|--|--|
| **ESS Pro** | `25.10.14+lts` | `26.4.9+lts` | `26.7.2` |
| **ESS Classic** | `25.10.09-gui` | `26.04.04-gui` | ⸻ |
| **ESS Community** | ⸻ | ⸻ | `26.7.2` |
| **ESS TI-Messenger** | `25.10.10` | `26.4.5` | `26.7.0` |

### Workarounds

Limiting request sizes or blocking the `multipart/form-data` content type before the requests reach Synapse, for example in a reverse proxy, alleviates the issue. Another approach that mitigates the attack is to use a low `max_upload_size` in Synapse.

### Identifiers

- ELEMENTSEC-2026-1740

### For more information
